source.title: Mechanistic Analysis Of Universality: Numerical Comparison Circuits Across Transformer Architectures
source.authors: Arya Bhardia; Julian Ramirez; Siddhanta Verma; Karen Mkrtchyan

record.file_problem: None; the complete paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: It tests whether task-specific circuits are consistent across model families and scales using causal patching and circuit analysis, rather than measuring representational-distance alignment.
record.gate_note: The study tests circuit-level universality for a numerical comparison task, not convergence of distances between representations. Benchmark accuracies are model-selection context, not alignment results. It does not test cross-modal alignment, seed variation, or representation mapping.
record.test_reason: It compares task circuits across six LLM checkpoints from three families. Using activation patching, PCA, path patching and DLA, it asks whether the same localized head-level circuit recurs. That bears directly on V5's claim that circuits recur across models. It does not measure representational similarity, so V1–V4, V6 and V7 are untested.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. Qwen models show a consistent localized head-level greater-than circuit. Llama3-8b-instruct and Gemma2-9b-instruct encode the signal earlier and more diffusely. Similar task accuracy therefore does not imply mechanistic universality.
record.recipe_differences: Uses activation patching, path patching, PCA, and direct logit attribution to compare task circuits; it does not measure representational-distance similarity as in the cited representation-convergence work. It studies one language task and six model checkpoints.
record.method_sensitivity: The circuit localization pattern varies by model family: Qwen models show a localized later-layer head signal, while Llama and Gemma show earlier, more distributed signal. The cross-model circuit comparison uses 4-digit prompts; the paper also reports Qwen2.5-3b patching at 2- and 8-digit lengths.
record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Student Research Workshop), 2026
record.problems: The study uses one numerical-comparison task and a limited set of six models. It could not identify specific components for path patching and neuron-level DLA in Llama or Gemma. The Qwen2.5-7b candidate head is inconsistently named in the main text and Table 7. No uncertainty estimates are stated for the reported patching scores.
record.rows_left_out: The remaining top-ranked head scores in Appendix Tables 2–9, other path-patching edges in Tables 10–13, neuron DLA rankings in Tables 14–15, and activation-steering plots are within-model circuit characterization rather than cross-model recurrence results. The figures for additional digit lengths in Qwen2.5-3b are not separately extracted because they concern within-model digit-length sensitivity, not the cross-model circuit comparison.

untested.parts: No cross-model representational similarity and no trend of alignment with scale or capability.
No vision models or paired image–caption data.
No mapping, stitching or relative representations between models.
Only one task (4-digit greater-than) is tested. Individual neurons or SAE features are not compared across models. Neuron DLA and path patching were not run in Llama or Gemma.
No comparison of similarity metrics or input distributions.
No measure of representational alignment and no test of shared data or objectives as its cause.

missing.what: Path-patching edges for Qwen2.5-7b and Qwen3-4b. Values are much smaller than in Qwen2.5-3b and Qwen3-1.7b, which weakens the claim that the branching structure is consistent across all Qwen models.

Qwen3-1.7b neuron DLA path patching. The heads feeding the top yes/no neurons are L17H11 and L17H9, not the two receiver heads L17H1 and L17H11. The authors call these contributions more distributed than in Qwen2.5-3b.

record.verdict_notes: The cross-model comparison is qualitative (PCA plots and text), with no uncertainty estimates. Recurrence holds only within one family sharing a training recipe, which is weak evidence for V5's 'different models'. The authors speculate that circuit localization depends on family or training, which is loosely related to V7, but they test nothing about representational alignment. The authors' 'not sharply distinguished' claim for Llama head scores is contradicted by Table 8.

versions.untested_parts: No cross-model representational-distance or similarity measurement, and no general test of representation convergence with scale or capability.
No vision models, paired image-caption inputs, or cross-modal alignment measurements.
No mapping between models, stitching, relative representations, or unpaired alignment.
Tests whether localized numerical-comparison circuit structures recur across six language-model checkpoints. It does not test recurrence of exact units, SAE features, or circuits across other tasks.
Does not compare representational similarity metrics, settings such as neighbour count, or in/out-of-distribution input choices.
Does not measure representational alignment or test whether shared data or objectives explain it. Its circuit-level findings bear on V5, not these proposed causes.

rows.subject: Qwen2.5-3b
rows.operation_detail: PCA and causal localization of the task signal in head outputs and residual-stream inputs.
rows.measure: Location and concentration of the separable greater-than signal
rows.value: The two selected Layer 24 heads' outputs separate clean and corrupt prompts; the Layer 24 residual input does not, while the downstream Layer 25 residual input does. The paper describes a localized, causally contributing head circuit.
rows.note: The paper treats this as a localized circuit; it does not establish that the exact heads recur in other models.

rows.subject: Qwen3-1.7b
rows.operation_detail: PCA and causal localization of the task signal in head outputs and residual-stream inputs.
rows.measure: Location and concentration of the separable greater-than signal
rows.value: Layer 17 head outputs separate clean and corrupt prompts; the Layer 17 residual input does not, while downstream residual inputs do. The paper reports a similar branching circuit structure to Qwen2.5-3b.
rows.note: The paper describes the structure as consistent within the tested Qwen models.

rows.subject: Qwen3-4b
rows.operation_detail: PCA and localization of the task signal in head outputs and residual-stream inputs.
rows.measure: Location and concentration of the separable greater-than signal
rows.value: Layer 22 head output shows the greater-than signal; the Layer 22 residual input does not show separation, while downstream residual layers do. The paper reports one relevant head rather than two.
rows.note: The paper describes the single head as having a role similar to the relevant heads in the other Qwen models.

source_check.correct: state=observed for the measured recurring localized greater-than signal. Layer22Head5 encodes the signal; Layer 22 residual inputs lack separation, while downstream inputs separate. One head rather than two changes circuit detail without making this signal partial.
source_check.problem: The partial state conflates a difference in head count with incomplete recurrence of the measured signal; R12 also reports a single candidate head as observed.

rows.check: The candidate head is Layer18Head15 (Table 7, Figs 10, 14, 20). The main-text name Layer18Head5 is a typo. The row's note implies the table is wrong; the reverse is true.

rows.subject: Llama3-8b-instruct
rows.operation_detail: PCA of residual-stream inputs and comparison of candidate-head patching scores.
rows.measure: Timing and concentration of the separable task signal
rows.value: Separable class structure is present in residual-stream inputs before the candidate head, emerging as early as Layer 13; candidate-head scores are not sharply distinguished, and the paper describes the computation as distributed.
rows.note: The authors say the candidate head propagates and amplifies an existing signal rather than generating it.

rows.note: The authors say the candidate head propagates and amplifies an existing signal rather than generating it.

relationships.reason: In each model, one or two mid-to-late heads write a PC1-separable greater-than signal that is absent in that layer's residual input and present downstream (R9, R10, R12).
relationships.display_finding: Each model had one or two mid-to-late heads introducing a PC1-separable greater-than signal absent from that layer's residual input and present downstream.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.reason: R9, R10 and R12 show localized head outputs containing a separable greater-than signal that is not separated in the corresponding residual inputs.

relationships.condition: Qwen3-4b, and the finer circuit structure within Qwen
relationships.reason: Qwen3-4b has one head rather than two (R11). Path-patching edges for Qwen3-4b (≤0.019, Table 13) and Qwen2.5-7b (≤0.062, Table 11) are far weaker than in Qwen2.5-3b and Qwen3-1.7b. So the claimed shared sender-branching structure is not clearly reproduced (text-based, no row).
relationships.display_finding: Qwen3-4b used one head rather than two, while path-patching effects ≤0.019 in Qwen3-4b and ≤0.062 in Qwen2.5-7b left shared sender branching unclear.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: Qwen3-4b, and the finer circuit structure within Qwen
source_check.reason: The finer wiring warrants qualification: Table 13 reports Qwen3-4b edges at most 0.01883 and Table 11 reports Qwen2.5-7b edges at most 0.0617, weaker than Tables 10 and 12. R11 nevertheless supports recurrence of the localized signal itself; one head alone does not establish partial recurrence.

relationships.reason: The task signal is already separable in the residual stream before the candidate head (Llama from Layer 13, Gemma around Layer 18). Gemma's head scores are flat. The authors conclude the Qwen circuit does not generalize across families (R13, R14, R8).
relationships.display_finding: The comparison signal preceded candidate heads from Llama layer 13 and around Gemma layer 18, with flat Gemma head scores, indicating that the Qwen circuit did not generalize across families.

source_check.label: challenges
source_check.reason: R13 and R14 show separable information before the candidate heads; R8 and Section 5 support distributed rather than sharply localized computation. The conclusion explicitly rejects generalization of the localized Qwen circuit to these families.
